table.title: [Departments of the Ministry of Agriculture, Commerce and Industry (Nungkungshangpu)]
table.caption_extra: Ministry of Agriculture, Commerce and Industry (Nungkungshangpu). ... Its work is conducted in four departments, whose duties are:

rows: Improvement and development of agriculture, afforestation, mulberry cultivation, cattle-breeding and preservation of wild animals, maritime industries, and the drainage and irrigation of agricultural land.
Fostering of industries and manufactures, inspection, development and supervision of mines, and the control of mining concessions.
Supervision and regulation of chambers of commerce, commercial exhibitions, monopolies, insurance and general commercial affairs.
Handling the income and expenditure of the Ministry, and supervision of the miscellaneous work of the Ministry.

transcriber_notes: Section heading and opening prose on p0269 (printed p. 230); the list itself is wholly on p0270. Four departments listed, matching the headnote.

table.title: [Departments of the Ministry of Posts and Communications (Yuchuanpu)]
table.caption_extra: Ministry of Posts and Communications (Yuchuanpu). ... Its work is performed in four departments, which supervise and control:

rows: Shipping, survey and sounding of harbours, organization of shipping companies and dockyards, lighthouses and buoys (which though nominally under this Ministry are still controlled by the Customs) and the revision and framing of shipping laws.
Railways generally, fixing of gauge, arrangement and repayment of railway loans, promotion of branch lines in the provinces, transport by rail, tramways, and the framing and revision of railway laws.

Telegraphs, government and commercial, framing and enforcement of telegraph regulations, agreements with foreign telegraph companies, telephones and electric light, and framing and revision of telegraph and telephone laws.
Posts, savings bank organized by the Post Office, money orders, parcel transport, design and issue of stamps, postal union agreements, and the framing and revision of postal laws.

transcriber_notes: Four departments listed, matching the headnote.

table.title: [Departments of the Ministry of Dependencies (Lifanpu)]
table.caption_extra: Ministry of Dependencies (Lifanpu). ... Its duties are performed by six departments, which supervise and control:

rows: The Eight Banners, and the bestowal of titles upon Mongolian bannermen.
Colonial administration, Mongolian hunting affairs, and the succession of Lamas.
Court ceremonial in connexion with the reception of tribute from the Dependencies.
Court ceremonial for the reception of Priests and Lamas.
Reception of Mohammedan delegations and tribute; hunting and agriculture in the Dependencies.
Punishments of and penalties exacted from Mongolians, Tibetans and Mohammedans.

transcriber_notes: Items 1-3 on p0270 (p. 231), items 4-6 on p0271 (p. 232). Six departments listed, matching the headnote.

table.title: [Sub-departments of the Department of Ceremonies (Tienliyuan)]
table.caption_extra: Department of Ceremonies (Tienliyuan). ... The work of the Department is carried on in four sub-departments, charged with the following duties:

rows: General Department, responsible for preparing Imperial prayers, and the custody of tablets, temples, mausolea, etc., and payment of officers employed in these duties; preparation of programmes for Court ceremonies, such as the conferring of titles upon members of the Imperial Family, weddings, etc., ceremonies to be observed on Imperial journeys, agricultural and sericultural ceremonies, custody of Imperial chairs, robes (including correct changes for the seasons) and supervision of gifts from the Throne to officials, and vice versa.

Imperial Worship and Sacrificial Department, which draws up the procedure to be observed during Imperial worship at various temples, including the form of worship, prepares lists of the Imperial escort, and of utensils for use on ceremonial occasions, and supervises the bestowal of tablets upon deceased princes, sacrifices to their spirits, and prepares Imperial ancestral tables.
A Routine Department, which prescribes the fasting to be observed by the Emperor, arranges for the reading of prayers, music for ceremonial occasions and dances.
The last department prepares lists of dishes for feasts, and superintends sacrificial offerings, wines, libations and animals, etc.

transcriber_notes: Four sub-departments listed, matching the headnote.

table.title: [Departments of the Revenue Council (Shuiwuchu)]
table.caption_extra: The Revenue Council (Shuiwuchu). ... The Shuiwuchu has four departments, which deal, respectively, with:

rows: Control of Imperial Maritime Customs Revenues on machinery and other manufactured goods and metals, Customs regulations, and the transmission of funds to Legations abroad.
The Native Customs, inspection of duty-free goods, collection of taxes upon salt, the revision of the tariff, and prevention of smuggling.
Collection of duties upon native and foreign opium, inspection of inland steam navigation, supervision of harbour-masters, lighthouses, and buoys, and the study of foreign tariffs.

Postal affairs (now handed over to the Yuchuanpu), appointments and rewards of Commissioners, appointments of officials under the Shuiwuchu, and the keeping of records of the services of all Customs officials, Chinese and foreign. This department is also responsible for auditing the expenses and income of the Customs.

footnotes: Several smaller departments deal with local Customs affairs.
transcriber_notes: Four departments listed, matching the headnote.

table.title: [Departments of the Imperial Board of Astronomy (Ch'intach'en)]
table.caption_extra: Imperial Board of Astronomy (Ch'intach'en). This Board predicts the climate, and studies the phenomena of the heavens in order to obey the heavenly signs. It is divided into four departments:

rows: Calendar Department, to draw up the calendar and indicate the auspicious days, calculate favourable days from the stars, etc.
Astronomy, which also undertakes to predict the future from heavenly phenomena.
Water-clock Department—a survival of the days when time was kept by water-clocks.
Instruction Department, for training students for future service under the Board.

transcriber_notes: Headnote says 'four departments' but five are listed (as printed).

table.title: [Principal officials in the provincial administration]
table.caption_extra: Provincial Administration. The principal officials in the provincial administration are:—

rows: or Governor General, who, except in the case of Chihli and Szechuan, rules two or more provinces. The Viceroy acts as Governor in the province in which his capital is situated, and controls the Governors of provinces within his jurisdiction. The memorial appended to this section defines in considerable detail the duties and responsibilities of Viceroys and Governors.
who is the executive head of a single province, in some cases being under a Viceroy, and in others having independent jurisdiction.
Commissioner of Treasury or Provincial Treasurer
who may be described as the Lieut. Governor, and is also in charge of the Provincial Exchequer, and is at the head of the Civil Service in the province.
a post which was created towards the end of the reign of the late Emperor to deal with the growing volume of business with foreigners at the provincial capitals.
who has replaced the old provincial Judge. His duties are fully defined in sections 12 and 13 of the attached memorial.
a Manchu official in charge of the Manchu garrisons in the province, and of Imperial Tombs, and other property. He ranks with the Viceroy, but the post is diminishing in importance.
whose duties are defined in sections 10–11 of the attached memorial.
who is Chief Comptroller of revenue derived from the Provincial Salt Gabelle.
who is Chief Comptroller of revenue derived from the grain tax, whether paid in money or in kind.
